channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Investors Brave Stock Market ‘Fragility’ as AI Trade Falters
item.description: The stomach-churning selloff that rocked equities has options traders girding for more volatility ahead.
item.dc:creator: Christian Dass and David Marino

item.title: Storm Devastates Rural Brazilian Town in Threat to Crops, Lives
item.description: A heavy storm that hit Brazil’s southern state of Rio Grande do Sul on Friday devastated a small town and raised concerns that continued rains and strong winds may bring further damage to crucial agriculture areas.
item.dc:creator: Dayanne Sousa

item.title: IQVIA Closes In on $1.1 Billion Takeover of UK Drug Services Group Quotient
item.description: IQVIA Holdings Inc. is closing in on a roughly $1.1 billion takeover of Quotient Sciences, as the US clinical research group looks to expand its role in bringing new medicines to market.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Gould and Michelle F. Davis

item.title: GTA VI Takes Over Thanksgiving Week
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg reporter Josyana Joshua tells host Lisa Mateo how the long-awaited release of Grand Theft Auto VI is becoming a cultural and workplace phenomenon, with gamers taking time off and preparing to play through Thanksgiving week. Joshua explains how the game’s 13-year buildup is driving demand for consoles and gaming gear while potentially competing with family gatherings, football and other holiday entertainment. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Fed’s Inflation Fight May Require More Hikes
item.description: Neil Dutta, head of US economic research at Renaissance Macro Research, tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the Federal Reserve made a mistake by holding rates steady in October and may need multiple hikes as inflation remains stubbornly above its 2% target. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Dutta says the recent market selloff does not yet signal broader economic trouble, arguing that AI investment and a resilient labor market continue to support growth even as the Fed has less flexibility to cushion falling markets. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Governors Push States to Lead on AI
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Governors Wes Moore, Spencer Cox, Josh Stein and Mike Braun tell host Christina Ruffini that states need to take a larger role in shaping AI and data center policy as concerns grow over electricity costs, water use, jobs and consumer protections. The bipartisan group says data centers should largely pay for their own energy needs and emphasizes local control, while differing over how aggressively the federal government should regulate AI. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Strong Earnings Prove No Match for the Crumbling AI Trade
item.description: For years, a strong earnings season has given Wall Street something to fall back on. But the crumbling artificial-intelligence trade has ripped away that support.
item.dc:creator: Geoffrey Morgan and Sagarika Jaisinghani

item.title: Oil Shock Response Sets Emerging-Market Bond Winners and Losers
item.description: Fuel subsidies are driving a widening divide in emerging markets, with investors favoring bonds from nations that have taken the painful steps to curb them.
item.dc:creator: Carolina Wilson, Nicolle Yapur and Mpho Hlakudi

item.title: Why Your Health Insurance Keeps Getting More Expensive
item.description: The average employer-sponsored family health plan now costs more than $28,000 a year, about the price of a new car, and premiums are expected to climb even faster in 2027. As costs rise, more of the bill is coming out of workers’ paychecks, and health care has become a top budget concern for CFOs. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump’s Asia Trip Leaves Key Issues Unresolved
item.description: ABC News State Department reporter Shannon Kingston tells Bloomberg This Weekend that Russia’s increasingly provocative actions near NATO countries are complicating President Donald Trump’s push for a negotiated end to the war in Ukraine, while Moscow remains publicly defiant. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Kingston says Trump’s Asia trip produced few concrete results and puts greater pressure on the upcoming G20 meetings to deliver progress on China, trade and other unresolved diplomatic issues. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Taiwan Mulls Lowering Margin Requirement to Support Stock Market
item.description: Taiwan is considering lowering the margin requirement ratio for stock investors using borrowed funds as it tries to stem a selloff after the benchmark equity index’s worst week in 35 years.
item.dc:creator: Miaojung Lin and Betty Hou

item.title: US Power Advantage Over China Shrinks Further on Iran War Effect
item.description: The advantage the US has over China in influencing the course of international events has shrunk to the smallest level since 2018, with the Iran war and unilateralism undermining its military and diplomatic strength, according to a new report.
item.dc:creator: James Mayger

item.title: Asia’s Stock Rescue Efforts Gather Pace After Wall Street Plunge
item.description: Asian authorities are stepping up efforts to stem a deepening stock-market rout, with China easing margin requirements, and Taiwan and South Korea rolling out intervention measures following Friday’s plunge in US equities.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: From Squeezes to Meltdown, a Week of Mayhem Rocks Metals Markets
item.description: As the copper industry gathered in Shanghai last week, Grace Li was struck by the overwhelmingly bearish mood over the outlook for demand. She agreed with the pessimism. In fact, she came close to pulling out her phone on the spot to put on a short position after her Monday conversations.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: S. Korea Rolls Out Phased Measures to Stabilize Stock Market
item.description: South Korea announced phased measures to calm markets amid rising volatility, including ensuring a stock stabilization fund is in place to respond when needed, top financial officials said after an emergency meeting on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Haram Lim

item.title: China’s $1.7 Trillion AI Rout Turns Hot Trade Into Losing Bet
item.description: China’s AI stock trade, once a hot bet as the nation’s technology powerhouses raced to catch up with the US, has morphed into a losing strategy.
item.dc:creator: Jeanny Yu and Winnie Hsu

item.title: Anthropic Fails to Calm AI Jitters, Ditching the Kitchen for Thanksgiving
item.description: The news doesn’t stop when markets close. Hosts David Gura, Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo bring clarity, context and a bit of humor to the weekend’s biggest headlines, LIVE from New York. Joined by Just Ice Tea Co-Founders Seth Goldman & Spike Mendelsohn, Seaport Research Partners Managing Director & Chief Equity Strategist Jonathan Golub, The New Yorker Staff Writer Jon Lee Anderson and The Atlantic Contributing Writer & “The Best Kind of American” Author Kim Ghattas. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Pointed! Bloomberg’s Weekly News Quiz For Risk-Takers
item.description: Pointed offers a strategic twist to the news quiz format, testing not just players’ knowledge of the news but also their confidence in their answers. Join Bloomberg’s Lisa Mateo, Christina Ruffini and David Gura as they play and check out the quiz for yourself at Bloomberg.com (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Russian Cargo Ship Attacked by Drones in Gulf of Finland
item.description: Russia said a cargo ship bound for its Kaliningrad exclave was targeted in international waters in the Gulf of Finland, highlighting growing risks to the country’s energy and food exports through critical Baltic Sea shipping routes.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News
